parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by resonance.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A small ball is held in place using a stretched string. One end of the string is fixed to a wall and the other end is attached to a vibration generator, as shown in Fig. 4.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Initially, the vibration generator is switched off.

A student displaces the ball vertically and then releases it. Fig. 4.2 shows the variation of the displacement of the ball with time after it is released.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text: State the name of the phenomenon illustrated by the decrease in the amplitude of the oscillations in Fig. 4.2.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain the decrease with time of the amplitude of the oscillations of the ball.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the frequency of the oscillations of the ball.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The vibration generator in (b) is switched on and its frequency *f* of vibration is gradually increased from 0 to 10 Hz.

On Fig. 4.3, sketch the variation with *f* for the amplitude of the oscillations of the ball.

[[fig:f3]]

figures.caption: Fig. 4.1
figures.alt: A ball attached to a stretched horizontal string between a vibration generator and a wall.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.2
figures.alt: A displacement–time graph showing oscillations with decreasing amplitude.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.3
figures.alt: A blank grid with amplitude on the vertical axis and frequency in hertz on the horizontal axis.
